title: Conformal Prediction
interviewAnswer: Conformal prediction wraps a predictive model to output sets or intervals with finite-sample marginal coverage under exchangeability; a calibration set determines the nonconformity-score quantile.
why: Conformal prediction is a practical way to add rigorous uncertainty to black-box models.
intuition: Instead of returning only a point estimate, return an interval calibrated to cover the target at a chosen long-run rate.
deepDive: Split conformal trains a base model, scores held-out calibration errors, selects a finite-sample corrected quantile and expands future predictions by that score. The guarantee is marginal, not automatically conditional for every subgroup.
commonMistakes: Saying each individual interval has a 90% probability guarantee after seeing x.
Using training examples improperly as calibration.
production: Monitor empirical coverage under distribution shift and use the sets to drive abstention/fallback when appropriate.
workedExample: Regression can use absolute calibration residuals to create prediction intervals around future predictions.

lab.goal: Build split-conformal regression intervals from held-out residuals.
lab.buildIt:
import numpy as np
rng=np.random.default_rng(0)
x=np.linspace(0,1,120); y=2*x+rng.normal(0,.15,len(x))
pred=2*x
cal=np.arange(80,100); test=np.arange(100,120)
scores=np.abs(y[cal]-pred[cal]); q=np.quantile(scores,.90,method="higher")
lo,hi=pred[test]-q,pred[test]+q
print(q,np.mean((y[test]>=lo)&(y[test]<=hi)))
